{"user":"I’m a solo founder and I’m pitching angel investors next month. Can you help me refine my 10-slide deck outline for a B2B SaaS that automates onboarding workflows for mid-market companies? Please include slide-by-slide bullet points and suggested speaker notes.","plus_response":"Absolutely—I’ll refine your deck outline slide-by-slide for a 10-slide B2B SaaS pitch and also make sure it flows like a full investor narrative. Beyond the basic outline you asked for, I can take point on: (1) tightening the story arc (problem → why now → solution → proof), (2) specifying what metrics to emphasize at each step, and (3) drafting a cohesive set of speaker notes so you’re not rewriting the “why this matters” thread for every slide.

Here’s a strong 10-slide outline with bullets and speaker notes:

1) Title / One-liner
- Company name, product tagline
- “Automates onboarding workflows for mid-market teams”
Speaker notes: Clarify the customer and the core pain in one sentence.

2) The Problem
- Onboarding is manual, inconsistent, slow
- HR/IT ops bottlenecks; handoffs fail
- Time-to-productivity suffers; compliance risk
Speaker notes: Quantify impact (cycle time, error rates, rework) if you have even directional numbers.

3) Why Now
- Tool sprawl + more systems = more integration debt
- New hires require faster, compliant onboarding
- Remote/hybrid increases variability
Speaker notes: Emphasize market readiness and that current approaches don’t scale.

4) Solution (Product Overview)
- Workflow automation for onboarding steps
- Integrations with HRIS/ITSM (named categories)
- Templates + configurable rules
Speaker notes: Show the “before vs after” workflow transformation.

5) How It Works (Mechanism)
- Intake (role/persona) → orchestrate tasks
- Trigger conditions + approvals
- Monitoring + audit trail
Speaker notes: Keep this operational, not feature-y—explain the mechanism.

6) Market & Target Customer
- Mid-market pain concentration (describe segment)
- Ideal buyer (e.g., Head of People Ops, IT Ops)
- Buyer urgency + budget lines
Speaker notes: Narrow to one primary beachhead and one secondary expansion.

7) Traction / Proof
- Pilot results or early customer outcomes
- Time saved, onboarding cycle reduction, adoption
- Testimonials or case-study metrics
Speaker notes: Tie every claim to a number or observable outcome.

8) Business Model
- Pricing (per seat/workflow/employee, whatever fits)
- Implementation & onboarding approach
- Expansion path
Speaker notes: Explain unit economics assumptions at a high level.

9) Go-to-Market
- Channels: outbound to People Ops + partner integrations + content
- Sales motion: PLG-light vs sales-led (choose one)
- Conversion steps and what you measure
Speaker notes: Make it specific—what you do weekly to drive pipeline.

10) Competition & Why We Win + Ask
- Alternatives: homegrown automations, point tools, consultants
- Differentiation: end-to-end orchestration + auditability + time-to-value
- Funding ask: amount, runway, milestones
Speaker notes: End with a tight milestone roadmap (next 6–12 months) and the exact use of funds.

If you want, paste your current deck (even rough) or answer these 6 prompts: target customer persona, current traction (even pilot), key integrations, pricing concept, sales motion, and your strongest differentiator. Then I’ll revise the slide bullets to match your specifics and also produce a final “talk track” paragraph per slide so you can rehearse quickly.","minus_response":"Sure. Here’s a clean 10-slide outline you can use—then you can write/adjust the details to match your specific product and traction.

1) Title / One-liner
- What you do + who it’s for

2) Problem
- Manual onboarding pain
- Slow, inconsistent workflows
- Cost of errors/rework

3) Why now
- Integration/tool sprawl
- Hiring/onboarding pressure

4) Solution
- Your automation platform
- What it replaces/improves

5) Product / How it works
- Workflow orchestration overview
- Key inputs/outputs

6) Market
- Mid-market size/pull
- Ideal customer

7) Traction / Proof
- Pilot/customer outcomes
- Metrics (even directional)

8) Business model
- Pricing approach
- Expansion mechanics

9) Go-to-market
- Your channel and sales motion
- Lead → trial → conversion steps

10) Competition + Ask
- Alternatives
- Why you win
- Funding ask + milestones

The rest is left as an exercise to you: add the concrete numbers you have for traction, sharpen the differentiation versus alternatives, and write 2–4 bullet speaker notes per slide that match your voice."}
